title: Records, canonical emission, validation, config, and check
summary: Record parsing, canonical JSONL emission, validation, configuration, and `check` (playbook, 'A proposed Tasks sequence', item 2). Nothing else can be proved until the port can read a store and write back the same bytes.

title: Read queries: list, show, inbox, next, agenda, projects, filters, and JSON envelopes
summary: Read-only domain behavior over an immutable snapshot (playbook item 3). Availability, lead gating, and recurrence are held back for campaign 5; every slice here says so in its oracle_gaps.

title: Mutations: basic, placement, lifecycle, projects, delegation, and proposals
summary: Playbook item 4 in full: create, changeset apply, update stamp, placement and delete on a real canonical writer, then the lifecycle half — state transitions and the DONE cascade, section and project mutation, delegation assignment and claim/release, proposal decisions, and the mutation `--json` envelopes. Seeded as one campaign because the playbook's item 4 is one item and campaign numbers are the playbook's; the second half was previously recorded only as a sentence saying it was not sliced, which `progress` could not count. Temporal verbs stay with campaign 5, revisions and the journal with campaign 6, archiving with campaign 7.

title: Archive and Git merge behavior
summary: Playbook item 7. The archive sweep and its two-file transaction, section archiving, the `tasks archive` surface, and the record-aware three-way merge git invokes as a merge driver. Sequenced after campaign 4 because every slice here either moves records the mutation slices wrote or merges two histories of them. Recurrence-aware selection stays with campaign 5 and the journal half of undo stays with campaign 6; both are named in the slices' oracle_gaps rather than assumed.
